headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy to propose cost allocation changes to shift certain infrastructure costs to large energy users, aiming to reduce the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large energy users.
news_headline: Virginia mulls shifting major grid costs to data centers.
news_summary: Virginia regulators are considering reallocating the multibillion-dollar cost of grid upgrades, currently spread across the public, to data center developers. The Governor's administration and consumer advocates argue data centers should pay for infrastructure driven by their demand.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires local water authorities to publicly report data centers' water consumption, increasing transparency regarding their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public.
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, mandates local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the information publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the industry's significant water consumption, particularly as it continues to grow.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high-energy use facilities, including data centers, to examine sound profiles and other environmental impacts on nearby residential areas and schools.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents, environmental advocates, Del. Josh Thomas.
news_headline: Data Center Bills Led 2026 Virginia General Assembly.
news_summary: The 2026 Virginia legislative session focused heavily on data center regulation, with HB 153 introducing new siting requirements for large data centers. This bill mandates impact assessments on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval, laying a foundation for stronger future regulations.
